# FDG9103

> DO represent ordered sequences as a separate type from their unordered counterpart.

Framework Design Guidelines, 3rd edition, section 9.6.5 Supporting LINQ through the Query Pattern.

## How it is checked

- Check: fdg (partial coverage)
- Diagnostics: FDG9103
- Automatic fix: not applied automatically (the fix can break callers)
- Severity: library warning, application warning, test none
- Status: draft

Message: Return an ordered sequence type from '{0}' that is separate from the unordered type '{1}'

The text has no body. FDG9103 reports a method of any accessibility named OrderBy or OrderByDescending, an instance method or an extension method, that takes a delegate or Expression<TDelegate> as for FDG9100 and returns the type it is applied to (the declaring type, or the type of its this parameter, by original definition) or IEnumerable<T>, the unordered sequence type of LINQ. Static methods that are not extension methods, and other methods that produce ordered sequences, are not checked, so coverage is partial. An OrderBy that returns the type it is applied to is not reported when that type is already an ordered sequence type: it implements IOrderedEnumerable<T> or IOrderedQueryable<T>, has an instance ThenBy or ThenByDescending query method on it, a base type or an interface it implements, or has an extension ThenBy or ThenByDescending in the class that declares the OrderBy. An extension ThenBy declared in another class is not seen, so such an OrderBy is still reported. Overrides and interface implementations are not reported. Changing the return type changes the public signature, so the fix is breaking; there is no code fix.
